newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to scrap cargo spacecraft next week.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to scrap cargo spacecraft next week.

text.p: Parts of an unmanned cargo spacecraft will soon drop into the Pacific Ocean after it failed to dock with the Mir space station this week, a senior Russian space official said on Friday.

Vladimir Solovyov, head of the space flights programme, said a special commission had approved the decision to scrap the Progress M-33 craft, most of which will burn up in the upper part of the Earth's atmosphere.
"We plan to do it between March 11 and 12. Some parts of the craft will fall into the Pacific," Solovyov told reporters at mission control near Moscow.

The Progress M-33, in orbit since November 1996, had de-docked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought up a replacement crew. But efforts to link it back to the mother ship have failed since then.
Solovyov said space engineers had been trying to dock the Progress with Mir to check a new docking system.

"It was an unsuccessful experiment, but we will repeat it with the next cargo ship because the new docking system is promising and it could be used with the new Alpha orbiting station," Solovyov said.
The Alpha space station, an ambitious international project, will replace the ageing Mir at the start of the next century.
Solovyov said the experiment would not affect Mir's space flight and said a scheduled U.S. shuttle launch due on March 15 would not be postponed because of the Progress' failure to dock.
The Progress M-33 had successfully delivered water, food, air and fuel to the Mir crew before it de-docked.
"There is only garbage from Mir now inside the craft," Solovyov said, adding that Progress currently had 196 kg (410 lb) of fuel to help it leave orbit.
The Progress' failure to dock marks the latest in a series of setbacks for Russia's financially troubled space programme.
On February 23, a fire broke out on board the 11-year-old Mir, forcing the crew, which at the time included a German and an American as well as four Russian, to don gas masks.
Solovyov told reporters on Friday that the fire had been caused by a faulty oxygen capsule.
He said the next cargo craft to supply the Mir crew, the Progress M-34, might be delayed because the rocket booster was not ready.
The launch is currently set for late March.
"The Mir crew has food, water and fuel until April 20 but we will send a cargo ship there before then," Solovyov added.
